column1: i|The word a person uses when talking about themselves.|I helped my friend carry the books.
i'll|A short way of saying I will.|I'll bring my favourite book to school.
ice|Water that has frozen solid.|The puddle turned to ice overnight.
illegal|Against the law.|It is illegal to take someone else's bicycle.
illegible|Too untidy or unclear to read.|The note became illegible after it got wet.
immature|Not fully grown or not behaving sensibly yet.|The immature apple was still small and green.
immediate|Happening straight away.|Our question got an immediate answer.
immortal|Able to live for ever, as in stories.|The immortal wizard lived in an ancient castle.
impatient|Finding it difficult to wait calmly.|The impatient puppy wanted its walk straight away.
imperfect|Having something that is not quite right.|I still loved my imperfect clay model.
inactive|Not moving, working or taking part.|The toy stayed inactive until we replaced its batteries.
incorrect|Not right or accurate.|I checked my incorrect answer and tried again.
increase|To become or make something greater.|The seeds increase in size as they grow.
incredible|So amazing that it is hard to believe.|The magician performed an incredible trick.
incredibly|In a way that is very great or surprising.|The new sunflower grew incredibly tall.
independence|Being able to do things or make choices yourself.|Learning to tie my laces gave me more independence.
independent|Able to do things or make choices yourself.|The independent reader chose her own book.
individual|One person or thing, considered on its own.|Each individual had a turn to speak.
infectious|Able to spread from one person to another.|Her infectious laughter made us all giggle.
information|Facts or details about something.|The sign gave us information about garden birds.
injection|Medicine put into the body with a small needle.|The nurse gave me an injection to keep me well.
innocence|Not having done anything wrong.|The missing biscuits were found, proving the puppy's innocence.
innocent|Not having done anything wrong.|The innocent puppy had not taken the biscuits.
instead|In place of something else.|I chose an apple instead of a pear.
interact|To do things or communicate with one another.|We interact by talking and playing together.
intercity|Travelling or running between cities.|We took an intercity train to visit our cousins.
interest|Wanting to know or learn about something.|The colourful insects caught my interest.
interfere|To get involved in a way that is not helpful.|Loud noise can interfere with quiet reading.
international|Involving more than one country.|Our school joined an international art project.
interrelated|Connected to one another.|Plants and insects are interrelated in a garden.
interrupt|To stop someone speaking or doing something for a moment.|I waited politely so I would not interrupt.
invasion|Entering a place in large numbers without being welcome.|An invasion of ants reached our picnic blanket.
invention|Something new that someone has thought of and made.|Our invention helped us water several plants at once.
irregular|Not following a usual pattern or shape.|The pebble had an irregular shape.
irrelevant|Not connected with what is being discussed.|The story about lunch was irrelevant to our maths question.
irresponsible|Not taking proper care or thinking about others.|Leaving litter in the park is irresponsible.
is|A form of be used to describe one thing.|The little bird is sitting on the fence.
isle|An island.|The small isle had a lighthouse.
jacket|A short coat worn over other clothes.|I put on my jacket before going outside.
jar|A container with a wide opening and a lid.|We kept our coloured beads in a jar.
jealous|Unhappy because someone has something you want.|The story's jealous squirrel wanted all the nuts.
jog|To run at a gentle, steady speed.|We jog around the field to warm up.
join|To put things together or become part of a group.|Would you like to join our drawing game?
july|The seventh month of the year.|Our school sports day is in July.
jumped|Pushed off the ground into the air.|The frog jumped onto a smooth stone.
jumper|A warm knitted top worn over other clothes.|I wore a cosy jumper on the cool morning.
jumping|Pushing off the ground into the air.|The children were jumping over small puddles.
june|The sixth month of the year.|The roses began to bloom in June.
kent|A county in south-east England.|We visited a farm in Kent.
key|An object used to open a lock.|I found the key to the garden gate.
kit|A set of things needed for an activity.|I packed my drawing kit for the trip.
kitchen|A room where food is prepared and cooked.|We helped to wash vegetables in the kitchen.
knee|The joint in the middle of your leg.|I bent my knee to tie my shoelace.
knight|A person in old stories who wears armour and serves a ruler.|The kind knight helped everyone cross the bridge.
knock|To tap or hit something to make a sound.|Please knock gently before opening the door.
knot|A tight loop made by tying string or rope.|I tied a knot to keep the parcel closed.
know|To have information or understand something.|I know where the reading books are kept.
lamb|A young sheep.|The little lamb stayed close to its mother.
language|Words and rules people use to communicate.|We learnt a greeting in another language.
lead|To show the way or be at the front.|Our teacher will lead us along the nature trail.
league|A group of teams that play matches against one another.|Our football team joined a local league.
led|Showed the way or was at the front.|Our teacher led us safely across the road.
legible|Clear enough to read.|My writing was legible and easy to follow.
leisure|Free time when you can relax and enjoy yourself.|I enjoy drawing in my leisure time.
library|A place where books can be read or borrowed.|We chose new books at the library.
licence|An official document giving permission to do something.|My aunt showed us her driving licence.
license|To give official permission to do something.|The council can license a business to sell food.
lie|To rest flat, or to say something untrue.|The puppy likes to lie on a soft blanket.
lightning|A bright flash of electricity in the sky.|We watched the lightning from safely indoors.
like|To enjoy something or think it is good.|I like reading funny stories with my friends.
limitation|A limit on what someone or something can do.|The tiny box's size was a limitation for our model.
live|To have your home somewhere or to be alive.|The rabbits live in a cosy burrow.
machine|An object with parts that work together to do a job.|The machine helped us make copies of our pictures.
made|Created or put something together.|We made a colourful card for our teacher.
magician|Someone who performs tricks that seem like magic.|The magician made a scarf appear from a hat.
mail|Letters and parcels sent to someone.|The mail arrived just before lunch.
main|The most important or largest part.|The main character in our story is a friendly fox.
male|A boy or man, or an animal of that sex.|The male blackbird had shiny black feathers.
malicious|Wanting to be unkind or cause trouble.|The story's malicious troll hid the bridge key.
man's|Belonging to one man.|The man's hat blew across the park.
mane|Long hair around a lion's neck or on a horse's neck.|The horse had a long brown mane.
many|A large number.|We found many different leaves in the park.
marvellous|Extremely good or wonderful.|We had a marvellous day at the seaside.
material|What something is made from.|We chose soft material for the puppet's coat.
mathematician|Someone who studies numbers, shapes and patterns.|The mathematician showed us a clever number puzzle.
me|The word used for the person who is speaking.|My friend saved a seat for me.
meant|Had a particular meaning or purpose.|I asked what the new word meant.
measure|To find the size, length or amount of something.|We used a ruler to measure our model bridge.
meat|Food that comes from an animal's body.|The dog had meat in its dinner bowl.
medal|An award, often worn on a ribbon.|She won a medal for her swimming.
meddle|To get involved in something that is not your task.|Please do not meddle with the model while it dries.
medicine|Something used to help someone feel better or treat illness.|The pharmacist explained how the medicine should be taken.
meet|To come together with someone.|We will meet our friends at the park gate.
megan's|Belonging to someone called Megan.|Megan's drawing had a bright yellow sun.
men's|Belonging to more than one man.|The men's boots were muddy after the walk.
mention|To speak or write briefly about something.|Please mention the picnic in your letter.
merriment|Fun and cheerful laughter.|The funny play filled the hall with merriment.
metal|A strong material such as iron or copper.|The gate was made from shiny metal.
mice's|Belonging to more than one mouse.|The mice's nest was hidden beneath the straw.
middle|The part between the beginning and end or between two sides.|Put the flower in the middle of the picture.
mind|The part of you that thinks, remembers and imagines.|I pictured the dragon clearly in my mind.
minute|A period of sixty seconds.|We had one minute to collect the counters.
misbehave|To behave in a way that breaks sensible rules.|The story's cheeky monkeys would sometimes misbehave.
mischievous|Playfully making small amounts of trouble.|The mischievous kitten hid inside the empty box.
mislead|To make someone think something that is not right.|The wrong arrow could mislead people on the trail.
miss|To fail to catch or reach something.|Try not to miss the ball when it rolls past.
missed|Did not catch, reach or notice something.|I missed the first bus but caught the next one.
misspell|To spell a word incorrectly.|It is easy to misspell a new word at first.
mist|Tiny water drops floating near the ground.|A light mist covered the field this morning.
monday|The day after Sunday and before Tuesday.|We visit the school library on Monday.
money|Coins, notes or amounts used to pay for things.|I saved my pocket money for a new book.
monkey|An animal with hands, often a long tail and a playful nature.|The monkey climbed high into the tree.
more|A greater amount or number.|We need more blue paint for the sky.
most|The greatest amount or number.|This tree has the most apples.
motion|Movement.|The wheels were in motion as the toy rolled along.
mountainous|Having many mountains.|The mountainous countryside looked beautiful from the train.
mourning|Feeling sad because someone has died.|The family was mourning their much-loved grandad.
mouth|The opening in your face used for eating and speaking.|I opened my mouth to sing the first note.
mr|A title used before a man's name.|Mr Brown helped us plant the seeds.
mrs|A title used before a married woman's name.|Mrs Patel read a story to our class.
muscle|A part inside the body that helps you move.|A muscle in my arm moved as I lifted the book.
musician|Someone who plays an instrument or makes music.|The musician played a cheerful tune on the flute.
my|Belonging to the person who is speaking.|I put my pencils in the blue pot.
mystery|Something puzzling that has not yet been explained.|We solved the mystery of the missing socks.
myth|An old traditional story, often about imaginary beings.|We read a myth about a flying horse.
national|Connected with a whole country.|We saw the national flag outside the building.
natural|Found in nature rather than made by people.|We used natural materials to build our model nest.
nature|The world of plants, animals and other living things.|We went on a walk to enjoy nature.
naughty|Behaving in a way that breaks rules or causes trouble.|The story's naughty squirrel hid everyone's hats.
near|Not far away.|We live near a park with tall trees.
new|Made, found or started recently.|I chose a new book from the library.
nicer|More pleasant or kind.|The game was nicer when everyone could join in.
nicest|The most pleasant or kind.|My friend gave me the nicest handmade card.
no|A word used to refuse or show that something is not so.|There were no pencils left in the pot.
nobly|In a brave, kind and honourable way.|The knight nobly offered to help the travellers.
nostril|One of the two openings in your nose.|The horse breathed gently through each nostril.
not|A word used to say that something is untrue or will not happen.|The paint is not dry yet.
notch|A small cut or dent in an edge.|The wooden block had a small notch in one side.
nothing|Not anything.|There was nothing left in the picnic basket.
notice|To become aware of something.|Did you notice the robin beside the gate?
noticeable|Easy to see or become aware of.|The bright new flower was noticeable in the garden.
nought|The number zero.|The score was three to nought.
now|At this moment.|We are ready to begin our game now.
nuisance|Someone or something that causes trouble or annoyance.|The buzzing fly was a nuisance during our picnic.
nutritious|Containing things that help your body stay healthy.|We packed a nutritious lunch for our trip.
obedience|Doing what a rule or instruction asks.|The puppy practised obedience during its training class.
obedient|Doing what a rule or instruction asks.|The obedient puppy sat when its owner asked.
obey|To follow a rule or instruction.|We obey the road safety rules on our walk.
observance|Following a rule or custom.|Observance of the playground rules helps everyone stay safe.
observant|Good at noticing things.|The observant child spotted tiny footprints in the mud.
observation|Something noticed by looking or listening carefully.|My observation was that the tallest plant had more sunlight.
obvious|Easy to see or understand.|The large red arrow made the answer obvious.
occasion|A particular time or special event.|The school concert was a happy occasion.
occupy|To fill or use a space.|The giant model will occupy the middle of the table.
occur|To happen.|Rainbows can occur when sunshine meets raindrops.
of|A word showing a connection or part of something.|I chose a piece of blue paper.
off|Away from something, or not switched on.|Please take your muddy shoes off at the door.
official|Agreed, approved or done by someone with authority.|The official start of the race was at noon.
often|Many times.|We often read stories together after lunch.
oil|A thick liquid that does not mix easily with water.|We added a little olive oil to the salad.
old|Having existed or lived for a long time.|The old tree had a wide, strong trunk.
only|Just one, or no more than what is mentioned.|There was only one red bead left.
opposite|On the other side, or completely different.|The library is opposite the park gate.
ordinary|Usual and not especially different.|An ordinary cardboard box became our pretend rocket.
other|Different from the one already mentioned.|Please put the other shoe beside the door.
ought|A word used to say what is a good idea or duty.|We ought to tidy the table before lunch.
our|Belonging to us.|Our class planted flowers beside the playground.
out|Away from the inside of something.|The rabbit peeped out of its burrow.
outrageous|Very surprising or shockingly unfair.|The story's giant made an outrageous demand for every biscuit.
own|Belonging to a particular person.|I wrote my own story about a friendly fox.
paid|Gave money for something.|We paid for the tickets before entering the museum.
pair|Two things that belong together.|I found a matching pair of socks.
parents|The people who bring up or care for their children.|The parents came to watch the school play.
parliament|The group of people who discuss and make a country's laws.|Our class learnt how parliament makes laws.
partial|Not complete, or showing a preference for one side.|A partial rainbow appeared above the trees.
particular|One specific thing, not any other.|I was looking for a particular blue pencil.
party|A gathering where people celebrate or enjoy themselves.|We played cheerful games at the birthday party.
passed|Went past something, or succeeded at a test.|We passed the library on our walk home.
patted|Touched gently with a flat hand.|I patted the friendly dog on its back.
patting|Touching gently with a flat hand.|My friend was patting the dog's soft head.
peace|A calm time without fighting or disturbance.|We enjoyed the peace of the quiet garden.
pear|A sweet fruit that is narrower at the top.|I chose a ripe pear for my snack.
peculiar|Unusual or strange.|The story's bird made a peculiar whistling sound.
pedal|A part you push with your foot to make something work.|I put my foot on the bicycle pedal.
pencil|A tool used for writing or drawing.|I drew a sunflower with my pencil.
penniless|Having no money.|The penniless traveller in the story was given a meal.
perceive|To notice or understand something.|I could perceive a faint sound behind the door.
perhaps|Maybe.|Perhaps we will see a rainbow after the rain.
permission|Being allowed to do something.|We asked permission before using the paints.
person|One human being.|Each person chose a colour for the picture.
persuade|To help someone agree by talking and giving reasons.|I will persuade my friends to try the new game.
phonics|Learning how letters and groups of letters represent sounds.|We used phonics to read the new word.
physical|Connected with the body or things you can touch.|Running is a physical activity I enjoy.
pie|A baked food with pastry around a filling.|We shared a warm apple pie.
piece|A part of something.|I used a small piece of paper for the flag.
plain|Simple and without decoration.|I decorated a plain box with colourful stars.
plainness|Having a simple appearance without decoration.|The plainness of the pot made its flower stand out.
plane|A vehicle that flies through the air.|The plane flew above the soft white clouds.
playful|Liking to play and have fun.|The playful kitten chased a rolling ball.
playground|An outdoor area where children can play.|We played a chasing game in the playground.
pleasure|A feeling of happiness or enjoyment.|Reading the funny story gave us great pleasure.
plentiful|Available in large amounts.|Wildflowers were plentiful beside the sunny path.
plough|A farm tool used to turn over the soil.|The farmer used a plough to prepare the field.
pocket|A small space in clothing used to carry things.|I found a smooth pebble in my pocket.
point|To show a direction with your finger or another object.|Please point to the largest tree on the map.
poisonous|Able to cause illness if eaten or touched.|Some wild berries are poisonous, so leave them.
politician|Someone who works in government and helps make decisions.|The politician visited our school to answer questions.
pool|An area of water where people can swim.|We practised swimming in the shallow pool.
poor|Having little money, or not of a good standard.|The story's poor woodcutter lived in a tiny cottage.
popular|Liked by many people.|The funny puppet show was popular with our class.
position|The place where someone or something is.|Mark the position of the treasure on the map.
possess|To have or own something.|The story's dragon hoped to possess the golden crown.
possession|Something someone owns, or the act of owning it.|My favourite possession is a book from my grandad.
possibly|Maybe or perhaps.|We could possibly visit the museum tomorrow.
potatoes|Vegetables that grow underground and can be cooked.|We dug up the potatoes from our garden.
precede|To come before something.|A short warm-up will precede the running race.
precious|Very valuable or important to someone.|The handmade card was precious to me.
preference|Liking one thing more than another.|My preference is to draw with coloured pencils.
preferring|Liking one thing more than another.|She chose blue, preferring it to red.
prejudice|An unfair opinion about someone before knowing them.|We learn to treat everyone kindly and challenge prejudice.
preparation|Getting ready for something.|Our preparation for the picnic included packing sandwiches.
pressure|A force pushing on something.|The clay changed shape under the pressure of my thumb.
principal|The main or most important person or thing.|The principal reason for our walk was to enjoy nature.
principle|An important rule or belief about how to behave.|Being fair is an important principle in our games.
privilege|A special opportunity or advantage.|It was a privilege to meet the author.
proceed|To go on or continue.|We can proceed with the game when everyone is ready.
profession|A type of work that needs special training.|Teaching is a profession that helps people learn.
profit|Money left after paying the costs of making or selling something.|Our pretend shop made a small profit.
programme|A planned set of activities, or a television show.|We watched a nature programme after school.
promise|To say firmly that you will do something.|I promise to take care of the library book.
pronunciation|The way a word is spoken.|We listened carefully to the pronunciation of the new word.
prophecy|A prediction about the future, often in a story.|The wizard read a prophecy about a brave traveller.
prophesy|To say what will happen in the future.|In the story, the owl could prophesy the weather.
prophet|Someone believed to speak about future events or religious messages.|The story's prophet spoke about a peaceful future.
prove|To show that something is true.|Our experiment will prove that the seed needs water.
pull|To move something towards you.|Please pull the drawer open gently.
purpose|The reason for doing or making something.|The purpose of the umbrella is to keep us dry.
push|To move something away by pressing on it.|We can push the toy car along the track.
put|To place something somewhere.|Please put your book on the shelf.
pyramid|A shape with a base and triangular sides meeting at a point.|We built a pyramid from small wooden blocks.
